gloss: food to accompany sake; drinking snacks

definitions.gloss: food served with sake; drinking snacks
definitions.explanation: dishes meant to be enjoyed while drinking alcohol
something to talk about during a drinking session (figurative)

examples.japanese: {枝豆|えだまめ}は{酒|さけ}の{肴|さかな}に{最適|さいてき}だ。
examples.english: Edamame is perfect as a drinking snack.

examples.japanese: この{刺身|さしみ}は{酒|さけ}の{肴|さかな}にぴったりだ。
examples.english: This sashimi is perfect to go with sake.

examples.japanese: {簡単|かんたん}な{酒|さけ}の{肴|さかな}を{作|つく}って{友人|ゆうじん}を{迎|むか}えた。
examples.english: I made some simple drinking snacks and welcomed my friend.

examples.japanese: その{失敗談|しっぱいだん}は{酒|さけ}の{肴|さかな}になった。
examples.english: That failure story became a topic of conversation while drinking.

examples.japanese: {昔話|むかしばなし}を{酒|さけ}の{肴|さかな}にして{飲|の}む。
examples.english: We drink while chatting about old times.

examples.japanese: あの{話|はなし}は{酒|さけ}の{肴|さかな}にしかならない。
examples.english: That story is only good for drinking conversation.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{肴|さかな} originally meant "food served with sake" before it came to mean "fish." The word {肴|さかな} is written with a different kanji (肴) than the common word for fish ({魚|さかな}).

SYNONYMS:
- おつまみ - drinking snacks (more casual)
- {酒肴|しゅこう} - drinking food (more formal/literary)
- あて - Kansai dialect for drinking snacks

COMMON DRINKING SNACKS IN JAPAN:
- {枝豆|えだまめ} (edamame)
- {焼|や}き{鳥|とり} (yakitori)
- {冷奴|ひややっこ} (cold tofu)
- {漬物|つけもの} (pickles)
- {刺身|さしみ} (sashimi)
